key_insight: CAMBY will investigate how brain network structure and function relate to persistent concussion symptoms in adolescents; it is not an AI or cancer drug discovery study.
clinical_relevance: The study could inform future targeted neurostimulation trials for persistent concussion symptoms, but it does not test a treatment.
method: Prospective observational study of adolescents aged 12–18 with a concussion history.
Collect MRI, MEG, and neuropsychological measures at least one month after concussion.
Compare persistent-symptom and recovered groups and test relationships among network microstructure, neural activity, and neuropsychological features.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a study protocol and planned analyses, with no participant counts or outcome results reported.
watch_item: Observational associations cannot establish that brain network alterations cause persistent symptoms or that targeting them will improve recovery.
paper_title: Concussion, Attention, and Mental Health: A Brain Network Study in Youth (CAMBY) - Study Protocol
